summary: Kshanika Saha is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned her PhD from the University of Calcutta (attested 1966), where she studied under Nalinaksha Dutt.

Kshetresh Chandra Chattopadhyaya (1896–1974) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Presidency University, Kolkata, the University of Calcutta, and the University of Allahabad. He held positions at Calcutta (~1919–1924), Allahabad (~1924–1956), and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1956–1968).

K. L. Dhammajoti (born 1949) is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at the University of Kelaniya. He held posts at Kelaniya, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, the University of Calgary, and the University of Hong Kong.

Kuladasa Karunadasa Jayatilleke (1920–1970) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera and at the University of Cambridge under Ludwig Wittgenstein, later serving as Senior Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Ceylon (attested 1963).

Kumataro Kawada (1899–1981) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1920–1923). He held faculty posts at Japan Women's University, Tokyo University of Literature and Science, the University of Tokyo (~1950–1960), and Komazawa University (~1960–1970).

Kun Chang (1917–2017) was a linguist, sinologist, and tibetologist who studied at Tsinghua University and under Franklin Edgerton. He held academic posts at the University of Washington (~1957–1963) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1963–1987).

Kunio Harikai (born 1942) is an Indologist and philosopher. He completed his BA and PhD degrees at Kyushu University, studying under Seiren Matsunami and Shoren Ihara, and served as Associate Professor at Saga Medical School (~1978–1996).

Kuno Lorenz (born 1932) is a philosopher who studied at the University of Kiel (~1958–1961). He held positions at the University of Hamburg (~1970–1974) and Saarland University, where he served as Professor (attested 2010).

Kuntala Bhattacharya is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from Jadavpur University (attested 2009) under Amita Chatterjee and Shyamapada Misra. She held an appointment at Rabindra Bharati University (attested 2009).

Kurt A. Behrendt (born 1964) works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1991–1997) and became an Assistant Curator at the Metropolitan Museum of Art (~2002).
Kurt Andrew Johnson is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of York under the supervision of Jane Moody, graduating by 2010.

Kurt Huber (1893–1943) was a philosopher who studied at Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium and the Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1913–1917). He later served on the faculty at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1920–1943).

Kurt Tropper is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna under Ernst Steinkellner. He has held posts at the University of Vienna and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Kurtis R. Schaeffer is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Washington and Harvard University. He has held academic posts at the University of Alabama (attested 2006) and the University of Virginia (~2005).
Kurunegoda Piyatissa (1929–2012) was a Buddhist studies figure who served as the head of the New York Buddhist Vihara (attested 1998, 2009).

Kwangsoo Park is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed an MA at the University of Iowa, earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and served as a professor at Wonkwang University (attested 2020).

Kyo Kano (born 1957) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Keio University, Kyoto University, and the University of Vienna, and has held positions at Kyoto University (attested 1989) and Kobe Women's University (attested 2000).
Kyojun Shimizutani (1891–1979) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at and held a post at Taisho University. He also served as head priest (貫主) of Sensō-ji (~1952–1979).

Kyoko Fujii (born 1948) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo. She held professorships at Yokohama City University, Hamamatsu University, Hokkaido University (~1996–2004), and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~2004–2018).
Kyoko Tokuno is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. She held a post at the University of Oregon and served as a professor at the University of Washington (attested 2017).
